message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: .NET Build

on: [push]

jobs:
  build:

    runs-on: windows-2022

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Setup .NET Core
      uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
      with:
        dotnet-version: 8.0.x
    - name: Cache NuGet packages
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.nuget/packages
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-${{ hashFiles('**/*.csproj', '**/packages.lock.json') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-
    - name: Build with dotnet
      run: dotnet build Website\\OCM.Web\\OCM.Web.csproj --configuration Release
",
  "rationale": "The workflow builds a .NET project on every push with no dependency cache, so NuGet packages are re-fetched on each run. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (dependency_cache) is supported evidence with a reported benefit and its preconditions are met: repeated dependency fetching occurs, and the cache key is pinned to repository inputs (runner OS plus hash of csproj/packages.lock.json) rather than unchecked build outputs. No equivalent cache already exists, and the cached NuGet package content is dependency-pinned, not mutable or untrusted. The change adds a single actions/cache step for ~/.nuget/packages before the build, leaving the build command, configuration, and required checks unchanged so intended build coverage is preserved.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
